State difference: recovery path vs. ordinary insertion path\n\n**Ordinary insertion** (`src/db/index/segment/segment.cc:903–918`): `Insert()` calls `append_wal(doc)` → `append_wal()` lazily opens the member handle `wal_file_` via `open_wal_file()` (`segment.cc:4324–4340`, `4303–4322`) → appends the record → then `internal_insert(doc)`. So after any write, two things hold: `wal_file_ != nullptr`, and the WAL file on disk (`<collection>/<seg_id>/<block_id>.wal`, `src/db/common/file_helper.h:74–78`) is larger than its 64-byte header, i.e. `has_record()` is true (`src/db/index/storage/wal/local_wal_file.h:75–77`).\n\n**Recovery path**: `CollectionImpl::Open` → `recovery()` (`src/db/collection.cc:308–329`, `1836–1892`) opens persisted segments read-only, then opens the writing segment whose meta still carries the `writing_forward_block` from the crashed version. `SegmentImpl::Open` calls `recover()` only when a writing block exists (`segment.cc:484–501`). `recover()` (`segment.cc:4193–4301`):\n\n- opens its **own local handle** `recover_wal_file` and closes it on scope exit (`segment.cc:4206–4215`);\n- replays each record through `internal_insert / internal_update / internal_upsert / internal_delete` (`segment.cc:4250–4266`) — the *internal* variants, which correctly avoid re-appending to the WAL but also **never touch the member `wal_file_`**.\n\nThe net state after recovery: recovered docs live in `doc_ids_`, `memory_store_`, the id map, and the in-memory indexers (`internal_insert`, `segment.cc:837–881`); the on-disk WAL still holds every record; but `wal_file_` (declared `nullptr` at `segment.cc:401`) remains **null**, because `open_wal_file()` is reachable only from `append_wal()`, which is called only from the public write APIs (`segment.cc:914, 932, 944, 968, 986`).\n\n**Why the data is initially readable:** every read path consults those in-memory structures, not disk. `doc_count()` is literally `doc_ids_.size()` (`segment.cc:589–599`), and `Stats()` sums `segment->doc_count(...)` over the live segment objects (`collection.cc:403–442`).
